title: Longest Palindromic Substring
keyIdea: Every palindrome has a middle: one letter or two. From each of the 2n − 1 middles, expand i left and j right while s[i] == s[j]; the last matching window is the longest palindrome with that middle. Keep the longest overall.

approaches.name: DP table
approaches.idea: dp[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] and (length ≤ 2 or dp[i + 1][j − 1]). Fill i from n − 1 down, j from i up; remember the longest true cell.
approaches.why: n(n + 1)/2 cells, each filled in O(1) from the cell diagonally inside it; the table itself is n × n.

approaches.name: Expand around center
approaches.idea: Your code: for each center, expand(center, center) for odd lengths and expand(center, center + 1) for even lengths; keep the longer result in maxi.
approaches.why: 2n − 1 middles, each expanding at most n/2 steps. Only a few indices are kept (passing s as const string& avoids copying it on every call).

quiz.q: Why expand from both (c, c) and (c, c + 1)?
options: Odd-length palindromes have one middle letter, even-length ones have two
To avoid going out of bounds
It's only needed for the last letter

options: It uses O(1) extra space instead of an n × n table
